properties.decision:
@ajs, 2026-10-06: "looking at this from a system of systems engineering problem, reflow2 is probably a 'component' of flo2 which is a system of integrated-flow (the system of systems level). Not sure if this is an important consideration in our 'hub' concept?" Then, on the reading below: "record it in reflow2's design as an accepted idea".

THE READING ACCEPTED:
- reflow2 is two things at once. A pinned build of reflow2 is a COMPONENT of flo2.io: flo2 runs it as its engine (0.79.0 on 2026-10-06). reflow2 the product is also a system in its own right: Anthony uses it at work without flo2, a team runs it on its own server, and integrated-flo requires it (req:each-subsystem-works-on-its-own). In system-of-systems terms that is operational and managerial independence, so reflow2 is a CONSTITUENT SYSTEM of integrated-flo, and flo2 USES it across an interface (its MCP surface, pinned to a version).
- So a hub's links are of two kinds, and the hub records which:
  · PART OF (the vertical tier, the y axis of dec:idea-design-is-composable-on-two-axes-authority-and-role): the member answers to the parent. Intent flows DOWN by allocation (a parent's requirement lands on the part). Status and evidence roll UP (a part's failing check puts the parent's capability at risk).
  · USES, ACROSS A NAMED INTERFACE (sideways, between peers): a change in the provider ripples ACROSS that interface to the user. The user may levy a requirement on the provider (dec:idea-gap-flows-to-the-dependency) but does not own its design.
  · A member can be both, as reflow2 is (a constituent of integrated-flo, and used by flo2).
- WHY IT MATTERS: the relation decides which way a change ripples and who sets requirements on whom. Today a hub's members are one untyped 'depends on' pin (external_dependency), so even a working cross-design ripple could not tell up, down or across; and if reflow2 were recorded only as 'part of flo2', flo2 would own reflow2's requirements, which is wrong, because reflow2 has stakeholders of its own.
- WHAT IT REFINES: dec:idea-a-graph-whose-children-are-themselves-reflow2-designs (settled 2026-09-26) says what a parent holds depends on whether its children are peer products (nothing) or the parts of one thing (more). This makes that distinction a RECORDED fact on each link, not a judgement made each time.
- HOW IT IS MEANT TO BE USED (not built; the hub-setup work after 2026-10-12): when a member is added to a hub, /hub asks 'is this a part of the parent, or a peer it uses, and across which interfaces?', records the answer, and runs link-projects for each named interface; the cross-design ripple (fact:root-cause-a-blast-radius-stops-at-its-design-by-design-and-nothing-says-where-it-left-2026-10-05; integrated-flo's root cause of 2026-10-06) follows PART OF up and down and USES across.
- THE CASES IT WAS CHECKED AGAINST: the dev_reflow2 hub (peer products, holds nothing: as settled); integrated-flo (the system-of-systems parent: its subsystems are PART OF it, and flo2 USES reflow2 across the tool surface); hxm_program at NSLS-II-style programs (projects PART OF the program, and one member USES another, as Planrunner uses hextools).
properties.name: ACCEPTED 2026-10-06 — a hub records HOW each member relates: PART OF the parent (a tier: intent flows down by allocation, status rolls up) or USES another across a named interface (a change ripples across; the user may ask, not dictate). A member can be both, and a cross-design ripple follows the relation
properties.rationale: Without the relation type, a hub is a flat list, and neither a ripple nor an allocation knows its direction. The systems-engineering distinction between a part (answerable to its parent) and a peer used across an interface is the one this owner works in, and it was already half-recorded in three open ideas and one settled decision; this names it once, on the link where every reader meets it.
